proposals.evidence: DEDR4798 gives Tamil/Malayalam māṭu ox and Kota māṛ beast, explicitly including cattle and buffalo. The southern survey maḍɨ/maḍu cow responses are comparative lect extensions of this cattle term, with a more specific female-bovine elicitation gloss than the Tamil/Malayalam ox gloss. Preserve that semantic difference and all original vowel-length/voicing notation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR816 gives Tamil erumai and Malayalam eruma/erima female buffalo, alongside Kannada/Kodagu emme. Irula/Kurumba ɛrumɛ/ɛramɛ are comparative southern-lect extensions preserving their vowels and source spacing; the elicited buffalo gloss does not itself specify sex. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR561 gives Kannada ugur, Tulu uguru, Kodagu oy and Kurukh orᵒx finger-nail. Survey uguru/ugarɨ and glide variants are comparative regional matches, with initial v-/a- and medial-y notation preserved. Kurukh orox matches the corrected rhotic spelling; the primary explicitly rejects Grignard’s oṛᵒx, so survey retroflex-r forms are held separately. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4635 gives Tamil mañcaḷ, Malayalam maññaḷ/mañña, Kannada mañjaḷa, Kodagu mañja and Tulu mañjaḷu turmeric or turmeric-yellow. The selected simple southern survey mañja/mañjal-type turmeric responses are comparative lect extensions preserving palatal nasal/stop spelling, final-lateral loss and vowel notation; no longer compound is reduced to this stem. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2020 gives Tamil/Malayalam cēṟu mud or mire, Kota cēr mud and Kannada kesaṟ wet soil/mud. These simple southern survey forms preserve the corresponding c-/s-/ts- and cēr-/kesar- shapes; minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions, not claims that each lect is individually listed. Source final central vowels and length notation are retained. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
